preheader: Anthropic chases a trillion-dollar IPO, inflation stays sticky, and Jannik Sinner targets a return.

lead.headline: Anthropic files an S-1 targeting a trillion-dollar valuation
lead.body: AI lab Anthropic has set a share price range of $70 to $78 for its massive initial public offering on the Nasdaq. The Claude maker is aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion, which would value the company between $1.02 trillion and $1.4 trillion. However, the filing reveals a staggering $900 billion in future computing commitments as the race for AI infrastructure intensifies.
lead.why: This is a masterclass in modern tech scaling and capital allocation. As a business student, watch how public markets price a company with massive revenue alongside near-trillion-dollar infrastructure liabilities.

stories.headline: Consumer inflation runs hotter than expected in October
stories.body: The consumer price index rose more than expected in October, signaling persistent pressure on the economy. The data gives the Federal Reserve difficult choices as officials weigh their next interest rate moves.
stories.why: Higher rates increase the cost of capital for startups and debt financing for acquisitions, which directly impacts private equity and investing deal flow.

stories.headline: Average new vehicle prices hit a record $51,109
stories.body: The average transaction price for a new car in the United States climbed to a record high of $51,109. Kelley Blue Book notes that buyers are responding by extending the length of their car loans to finance the purchases.
stories.why: Consumer credit trends like stretched auto loans give you a real-world look at how everyday household debt expands when baseline costs rise.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares see heavy retail dip-buying after scandal
stories.body: Retail investors poured capital into Nvidia stock, surging purchases by over 400 percent after shares dropped following reports regarding CEO Jensen Huang. Despite the executive distraction, analysts view the long-term chip replacement cycle as intact.
stories.why: Market sell-offs driven by headlines often create classic buy-the-dip moments. It is a textbook study in separating short-term noise from a company's underlying fundamentals.

stories.headline: TSMC invests up to $1 billion across Anthropic and OpenAI
stories.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company plans to invest up to $1 billion across leading AI developers Anthropic and OpenAI. The move highlights the chipmaker's confidence in long-term demand despite broader market anxiety over soaring AI spending.
stories.why: When a picks-and-shovels manufacturer invests directly in its own customers, it signals immense conviction in the supply chain's multi-year revenue visibility.

stories.headline: Boston Consulting Group tapped for UK government strategy
stories.body: Boston Consulting Group has been hired by the UK government to advise on its upcoming 10-year national strategy. The engagement highlights the continued reliance of public sector entities on top-tier strategy firms.
stories.why: If you are targeting a career in management consulting, keeping tabs on major public sector wins shows where top firms are capturing long-term advisory fees.

stories.headline: Gen Z founders bypass entry-level corporate jobs for AI startups
stories.body: A growing number of young professionals are skipping traditional entry-level corporate roles to launch their own companies. Artificial intelligence tools have dramatically lowered the technical barrier and cost required to build a minimum viable product.
stories.why: This is your exact peer group. It proves you don't need a decade of corporate experience anymore to spin up a tech-enabled venture right out of college.

stories.headline: UC Irvine included in new $38.2 million climate research initiative
stories.body: The University of California launched the Climate Change Research and Policy Institute, an initiative funding work to be conducted across UC Irvine, UCLA, UC Santa Barbara, and UC Davis.

stories.headline: Jannik Sinner targets Australian Open comeback
stories.body: Former world number one Jannik Sinner confirmed he is targeting the Australian Open in January for his return to competitive tennis. Sinner has been sidelined since July due to a knee injury.

term.name: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
term.definition: A broad economic gauge that measures the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of consumer goods and services. Central banks use it as a primary benchmark to track inflation and determine interest rate policy. When the CPI rises faster than expected, it often prompts the Federal Reserve to keep borrowing costs elevated.

serve.headline: Bay raised $50 million to help companies secure AI agents
serve.body: Israeli cybersecurity startup Bay secured $50 million in early funding led by Battery Ventures to help enterprises deploy and manage secure AI agents. The company has spent less than a year operating in stealth with dozens of corporate clients.
